solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Food item in batter served with old port

blocks.note: a club is something to batter with, or to club is to batter
Sandwich in Kent was one of the medieval Cinque Ports, now silted up and inland

explanation.surface: Something deep-fried in batter is served alongside a glass of vintage port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' pretends to be the coating for fried food; it is the verb, or the weapon that batters. Sandwich is a Kent town that was a port in the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A multi-decker sandwich with layered fillings is a classic snack served on lunch menus.

clue.text: A punch absorbed by part of the body, draining

indicators.note: what is absorbed ends up inside something else, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw
the leg is a limb

explanation.surface: A body blow is soaked up by the torso, leaving the boxer drained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' reads as a noun, but here it is the slangy verb to chin, meaning hit on the jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaching is the slow removal of substances by water percolating through, an emptying or seeping process.

clue.text: Champion defender

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to support or promote a cause
second meaning: in football or hockey, a player in a defensive position

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a title-holding defender; 'Champion' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To support a cause is to champion it, and a full-back or centre-back is a defensive player in team sports.

clue.text: For cooking, heated tray available now

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, and cooked-up letters are rearranged into something new

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A warmed baking tray is ready to use for cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture makes 'For cooking' look like a description of the tray's purpose, not the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prepared for immediate use is waiting in position, prepared to be used without delay.

clue.text: Collecting boundaries in cricket, opener W. G. Grace, perhaps?

indicators.note: boundaries are the edges of something, so only the outermost letters are wanted
to collect is to gather in, so one piece takes another inside it

blocks.note: a door is what opens a way in
first and last letters of cricket

explanation.surface: W. G. Grace, the great batsman who opened the innings, piles up fours and sixes.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a four or six, and an opener is an opening batsman, so the whole surface stays on the pitch. W. G. Grace was a famous Victorian English cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace qualified in medicine and practised as a physician, so he is an example of a medical man; the question mark signals the example.

clue.text: Visiting country briefly, taking in island first

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short, losing its final letter
to take in is to admit inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: someone visiting is in, at the place
a country
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: On a short trip abroad, the traveller calls at an island before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: Italy loses its last letter, then the island goes between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial as an adjective means occurring at the beginning, earliest in a sequence.

clue.text: Last part in hand

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
in poker, a straight is a hand of five cards in sequence

explanation.surface: The final section is already in hand, nearly secured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hand' looks like a set phrase meaning under control; split it, and each word yields a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The home straight is the final stretch of a racecourse before the finishing post, hence the closing stage of anything.

clue.text: Book Church of England extracted from novels

indicators.note: what is extracted is pulled out and taken away, leaving the rest

blocks.note: romances are novels of love or adventure
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Anglican text is quoted out of a pile of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed letters come out of the middle of the longer word, not from an end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle to the Romans is a book of the New Testament, written by Paul.

clue.text: Star runner running backwards

indicators.note: going backwards means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: a runner is a river in crosswords, and the Avon is an English river

explanation.surface: A star athlete runs the wrong way round the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star runner' suggests a champion athlete; the star is the definition and the runner is a river, something that runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly brightens enormously for a short period before fading back.

clue.text: Religious teaching restored ethics in University briefly

indicators.note: something restored is rebuilt or reworked, so the letters are put together afresh
one piece sitting in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: Cambridge University shortened, as in Oxbridge usage 'Cantab' and the river Cam
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Moral philosophy is briefly revived at a university as part of religious instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge is cut down to its first three letters; the rearranged moral word goes between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism is a summary of Christian doctrine set out as questions and answers for instruction.

clue.text: Look at notes and accept what must happen?

blocks.note: first meaning, taken literally: to turn toward the written score in front of you
second meaning: the idiom for confronting the unpleasant consequences of your actions

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a literal, whimsical reading of the idiom: to face something is to look at it, and music is written notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to confront criticism or punishment you have earned, taking consequences bravely.

clue.text: Native American swiftly lassoing horse’s head

indicators.note: a head is at the top or front, so only the first letter is wanted
a lasso loops around and catches something, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: apace means at speed
first letter of horse

explanation.surface: A rider of the plains quickly ropes a horse by the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse's head' is the first letter, not a noun; the lasso picture fits the cowboy scene perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a group of Indigenous peoples of the south-western United States.

clue.text: Insects that pollinate about a hundred and one flowers

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the others

blocks.note: bees are insects
a ton is slang for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Bees pollinate roughly a hundred and one flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About a hundred and one' reads as an approximate number; 'about' is the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Betony is a purple-flowered plant of the mint family, formerly used in herbal medicine.

clue.text: Description of some trees of course, in ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, so the letters are broken down and remade

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A remark that some trees are, naturally, rooted in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' sounds like a casual aside; it is most of the fodder, and 'ground' is the verb grind, not soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Coniferous describes cone-bearing trees such as pines and firs, typically evergreen.

clue.text: Incompetent one, where is US president?

indicators.note: something handled incompetently is botched and messed up, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone useless asks where the American president has got to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incompetent one' looks like a noun phrase for a fool; the adjective is the signal and 'one' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight D. Eisenhower was the 34th holder of the American presidency, serving 1953 to 1961.

clue.text: As a cloudless sky not entirely right, it’s not clear

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: a blur is something not clear

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a cloudless sky is blue
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The sky is not perfectly cloudless, so the view is hazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely right' tempts as a phrase; 'not entirely' trims the colour, and 'right' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is an indistinct shape or image, something seen without sharp focus.

clue.text: Hopeful nation in a bit of difficulty, with nothing to lose

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
what is lost is taken away, so a letter disappears

blocks.note: taken as written
Iran is a nation
a spot of bother is a bit of trouble
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A hopeful country in some trouble has nothing left to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: The nation goes inside the small trouble word, then its O drops out; the leading A stands alone. 'Hopeful' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone who aims for a position or success, a candidate with ambitions.

clue.text: Army entertainer

blocks.note: first meaning: a large multitude, especially an army
second meaning: a person who entertains guests

explanation.walkthrough: 'Army entertainer' suggests someone who performs for troops; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a great multitude or armed force, and also the person receiving and looking after guests.

clue.text: Weapon is raised, well sawn off!

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising letters lifts them upward, so they read bottom to top
sawn off means cut short, so the end is lopped away

blocks.note: taken as written
'Well!' and 'dear me!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A gun is lifted up — goodness, it's a sawn-off shotgun!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' is the exclamation, rendered as two words and then docked of its last letter; 'sawn off' echoes the sawn-off shotgun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a pistol or sword worn at the hip, a personal weapon carried by soldiers or police.

clue.text: Indian thus translated — in his own words?

definitions.note: a cryptic phrase standing for the name of a language

indicators.note: translating turns something into a different form, so the letters are converted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An Indian's speech rendered into his own tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translated' fits the language theme, but it is the signal; the definition asks what an Indian speaks in his own words.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindustani is the language family of northern India covering Hindi and Urdu, so it is his native speech.

clue.text: Beast tethered by Peruvian, I’m a llama!

indicators.note: something tethered is held fast by the words around it, so the letters lie within them

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word and into the next three

explanation.surface: A tied-up llama from Peru announces what kind of creature it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The beast in the scene is the llama, which is also where half the letters sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Beast is a general term for a creature, especially a four-footed mammal.

clue.text: Willing to sit upon the empty egg perhaps?

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on top means coming first, above what follows
emptied of its middle, a word keeps only its outer letters

blocks.note: game means willing, up for it
first and last letters of the

explanation.surface: A broody hen is willing to sit on an egg even if it holds nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The hen picture makes 'sit upon' sound like brooding; in a down clue it places one piece above another.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamete is a reproductive cell; an ovum is an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Journalist, one coming between friends tries to make things work

indicators.note: coming between means entering the middle, so pieces go inside another

blocks.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
I is the Roman numeral for one
mates are friends

explanation.surface: A reporter who steps into a quarrel between friends tries to patch things up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's go-between is exactly what the answer means, so it reads almost as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: To mediate is to intervene between parties in a dispute, trying to bring about agreement.

clue.text: Sound of European torpedo

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken, so its pronunciation matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: a Finnish person is a European from Finland

explanation.surface: The noise made by a torpedo fired from a European submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torpedo' is a verb here: to wreck or scupper a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo a plan is to destroy it, putting an end to it completely.

clue.text: Prison service talking in riddles, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the first letters of the words are taken

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: The prison service speaks in riddles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prison service' looks like one phrase; only 'Prison' is the definition, and 'service' starts the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is old British slang for jail, as in doing time behind bars.

clue.text: High, a long distance apart

blocks.note: first meaning: dazed or intoxicated, as if on drugs
second meaning: arranged with wide gaps between

explanation.walkthrough: 'High' first suggests tall or elevated, which chimes with distance; it is the drug-slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means dazed or euphoric from drugs, and also placed at wide intervals from one another.

clue.text: First male, a female

blocks.note: taken as written
breeders call an animal's mother, especially a mare, by this word

explanation.surface: The first man and a woman: the Eden story in miniature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female' suggests Eve; dam is the breeders' word for an animal's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam is the earliest man created by God, father of humankind.

clue.text: The same meat runs out during visit

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged
during means within a span, so one piece falls inside another

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
to come is to visit, as in come round

explanation.surface: Same menu again: the meat has run out while you are visiting.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters go between the third and fourth letters of the visiting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Commensurate means corresponding in size or degree, proportionate, equal in measure.
